title: Penalized prediction model development with bootstrap optimism correction
summary: Ridge logistic regression with a cross-validated penalty, and Harrell's bootstrap correction of the apparent AUC and calibration slope, checked against an external validation cohort.

sizing._why: Prediction-model development is sized by the Riley et al. (2019) criteria (shrinkage, optimism, precision of the intercept); no catalog form implements them, and events-per-variable is only a floor.

pinned_defaults: Ridge (L2) logistic regression on predictors standardized within each fit (SD with n - 1), intercept unpenalized; objective loglik - (lambda / 2) sum(beta^2); Newton-Raphson to 1e-12, written out in both languages. glmnet and scikit-learn scale the penalty differently (glmnet divides by n; scikit-learn uses C = 1 / lambda) and use their own solvers.
Penalty chosen by 5-fold cross-validated deviance over 12 values log-spaced from 0.1 to 100; folds fixed in the fixture.

Harrell's bootstrap optimism correction with every step repeated in each resample, including the cross-validated penalty choice (folds by position within the resample). 50 resamples, supplied by the fixture (bootstrap.csv) so both languages use the same ones; in practice use 200 or more.
Calibration slope: coefficient of the linear predictor in a logistic regression of the outcome on it.
_what_is_checked: Over 100 seeds the apparent AUC exceeds the external cohort's by 0.033 on average and the corrected AUC by -0.0015; the apparent slope by 0.20 and the corrected slope by 0.0006. The correction is unbiased, but in a single development sample it is imprecise (the corrected-minus-external AUC ranges to 0.09), which is why its recovery tolerances are wide and the mean-bias assertions carry the check.
_riley: 68 events for 10 candidate predictors is below the Riley criteria; the fixture is small on purpose, to make the optimism visible.
